title: Manetta hired for the St. Louis boat band, Bob Sharper and Ed Allen
summary: Manetta recalls being sent for from St. Louis, insisting Desvigne be taken too, the leadership passing from Sharper to Eddie Allen, and arriving in St. Louis.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: No, they sent to me, coming from St. Louis. But on Easter Monday morning, you see? You know, when I gave him my award, they were going to organize a band. And sent for me to come and meet the both, coming in the office. Well, I gave them my award. And the time didn't come, he wrote, that is, the road last time. And so, uh... We, uh... We played with Oak, Dad. That's San Suo Hall. You remember that? Well... All right. I said, I showed Sidney the telegram on Monday night. You remember San Suo Hall? You forgot that? No, I remember.
We go down to the telephone exchange. And he was right there. Yeah, Holtz.

Get him to take me. And I agreed, I said, well, I'll answer a little bit. I said, if you're free to take trumpet players, it's a dance game. Well, they had a rope in the back. So, I don't know. I've seen that white thing before. And I didn't see it. So, they're great, Ted. So, uh... I went along when the time come. I had the band all made up. They had Bob Sharper. Was the leader of the band. I taught this out in Ed Allen up there. So, they had a... They had a lady I was playing the piano with. Until I... Go with him. Go with him. I'm getting a little bit of a question. So... When I agreed to go, unless they take Sydney.
You've been working, you say, at the Cotton Building, was that? Or something like that? They had a way in town. At a day job. Yeah.

So, what I did, while they go to the Wake, they get me there, Bob Sharper go. Bob Sharper turned the leadership over to Eddie Allen. And that made a hard feelings. That made a hard feeling. But when I go to St. Louis, Sidney didn't go to me, but... I go to St. Louis, when this guy, Captain, I want him to come to meet me at the train. At the train. At the train, the guy would say hello to me and all that, but he knew that I was the fella that he was looking for. You know, they had them big old-looking mind glasses. You know, I'll put... I'd like to know where the... Mel Pottson Building is at. Who are you? I told him, he said, Well, I come out here and wait for you. You're going to be the piano brother, yeah. So, the outbrain, he said, where to stop at. So, he carried me. Johnny Sensei and George Foster was living together. On that morning, Johnny Sensei had his son. His wife had a boy. He's now about... Boy must be now around about 39, ain't he?
This guy has a good memory, you know that?
George Foster and Johnny Sensei was living together in the house. We go back in the kitchen. This fella just that bit. See, they're right there. Oh.
